problem_statement: Add a new ztimer64 module that provides a 64-bit timer API backed by an existing 32-bit ztimer clock. It must provide the types and functions used by the new unit tests: ztimer64_clock_t, ztimer64_t with callback and arg fields, ztimer64_clock_init(ztimer64_clock_t *, ztimer_clock_t *), ztimer64_now(ztimer64_clock_t *), ztimer64_set(ztimer64_clock_t *, ztimer64_t *, uint64_t), ztimer64_set_at(ztimer64_clock_t *, ztimer64_t *, uint64_t), and ztimer64_remove(ztimer64_clock_t *, ztimer64_t *). ztimer64_clock_init() initializes a 64-bit clock from a 32-bit ztimer clock. ztimer64_now() returns a 64-bit timestamp that advances through normal overflows of the 32-bit backend, while matching the expected behavior for very large backend jumps where the 64-bit time may remain unchanged. ztimer64_set() schedules the timer callback after a relative offset, including offsets greater than 2^32; ztimer64_set_at() schedules at an absolute timestamp and must trigger as soon as possible if that timestamp is already in the past; a zero relative offset must also trigger as soon as possible. ztimer64_remove() cancels a pending timer so it no longer fires.

verification.reason: The statement only covers unit-test requirements but the hidden tests also include an integration test needing additional public interface elements (sub-modules, Kconfig option, global instances, two additional functions, module flags). All gaps are fixable by expanding the statement to describe the full public interface the tests exercise.

problems.detail: The statement scopes requirements to 'the new unit tests' but the hidden tests also include an integration test (tests/ztimer64_msg/) that requires additional modules, functions, Kconfig options, and global instances not mentioned in the statement.

The integration test uses CONFIG_ZTIMER64_USEC (Kconfig option), ztimer64_usec (module), ZTIMER64_USEC/ZTIMER64_MSEC/ZTIMER64_SEC (global clock instances), ztimer64_sleep(), ztimer64_set_msg(), and MODULE_ZTIMER64_SEC/MODULE_ZTIMER64_MSEC (module flags for conditional compilation), none of which are mentioned in the statement.

The integration test exercises ztimer64_sleep() (puts calling thread to sleep for a duration) and ztimer64_set_msg() (sets a timer that sends a message to a pid), behaviors not described in the statement.

leak_check.missing: The exact overflow/checkpoint behavior of ztimer64_now is only described vaguely, and the Kconfig/module wiring for MSEC/SEC is less precise.

problem_statement_fixed: Add a new ztimer64 module that provides a 64-bit timer API backed by an existing 32-bit ztimer clock. It must provide the types and functions: ztimer64_clock_t, ztimer64_t with callback and arg fields, ztimer64_clock_init(ztimer64_clock_t *, ztimer_clock_t *), ztimer64_now(ztimer64_clock_t *), ztimer64_set(ztimer64_clock_t *, ztimer64_t *, uint64_t), ztimer64_set_at(ztimer64_clock_t *, ztimer64_t *, uint64_t), ztimer64_remove(ztimer64_clock_t *, ztimer64_t *), ztimer64_set_msg(ztimer64_clock_t *, ztimer64_t *, uint64_t, msg_t *, kernel_pid_t), and ztimer64_sleep(ztimer64_clock_t *, uint64_t). ztimer64_clock_init() initializes a 64-bit clock from a 32-bit ztimer clock. ztimer64_now() returns a 64-bit timestamp that advances through normal overflows of the 32-bit backend, while matching the expected behavior for very large backend jumps where the 64-bit time may remain unchanged. ztimer64_set() schedules the timer callback after a relative offset, including offsets greater than 2^32; ztimer64_set_at() schedules at an absolute timestamp and must trigger as soon as possible if that timestamp is already in the past; a zero relative offset must also trigger as soon as possible. ztimer64_remove() cancels a pending timer so it no longer fires. ztimer64_set_msg() schedules delivery of a message to a target thread after a relative offset. ztimer64_sleep() suspends the calling thread for the given duration in the clock's tick units. The module must provide ZTIMER64_USEC, ZTIMER64_MSEC, and ZTIMER64_SEC as extern pointers to initialized ztimer64_clock_t instances, available through build modules ztimer64_usec, ztimer64_msec, and ztimer64_sec with corresponding Kconfig options CONFIG_ZTIMER64_USEC, CONFIG_ZTIMER64_MSEC, and CONFIG_ZTIMER64_SEC. Enabling any of these options must cause the corresponding ztimer64 clock to be initialized from the matching 32-bit ztimer clock (ZTIMER_USEC, ZTIMER_MSEC, ZTIMER_SEC respectively).
